leads.name: Golden Weeping Ash (Guldhængeask), Landbohøjskolens Have
leads.location_hint: South Garden (Sydhaven), facing Bülowsvej, Landbohøjskolens Have, Frederiksberg
leads.reason: Single-sourced: only kub.ku.dk's 2008 historical feature ('De gamle traeer i fakultetets have') describes it, ~150 years old at time of writing (so ~168 now), 4 m tall. No independent second source found for age or survival, and no other outlet mentions it by name. Also modest and unspectacular in stature ('despite modest size, has endured'), so it may not clear the visually-spectacular/historically-significant bar even if a second source turns up. Worth a direct query to the garden.

leads.reason: Only the same single kub.ku.dk 2008 article describes it; no age given, no second source, no coordinates beyond a vague garden-internal reference.

leads.location_hint: facing Bülowsvej, Landbohøjskolens Have, Frederiksberg

leads.name: Wingnut (vingevalnød / Pterocarya) at Allégade, Frederiksberg
leads.location_hint: park area near Allégade, Frederiksberg (exact spot not found)
leads.reason: Cited by frederiksberg.dk-linked search summaries as 'approximately 200 years old, one of the municipality's oldest trees' but the source page that stated this could not be located directly (404 on the most likely URL); no second independent source, no coordinates, no confirmation the tree still stands. Needs a fresh search for the current frederiksberg.dk page or a call to the municipality's tree register.

leads.name: Lindens of Frederiksberg Slot garden
leads.location_hint: Frederiksberg Slot grounds, Frederiksberg
leads.reason: Described in passing by search summaries as 'the state's 300-year-old linden trees at Frederiksberg Slot', Denmark's oldest trees on Frederiksberg, but no primary source found describing them individually. Access is a real problem: the palace now houses the Army Officers' School (Haerens Officerskole) and is open for guided tours only about ten days a year (last Saturday of the month, per migogkbh.dk), so even if verified this would ship as 'restricted' access at best, not a casual walk-up. Needs a Slots- og Kulturstyrelsen or Forsvaret source with real detail before pursuing further.

leads.name: Giant plane tree, Assistens Kirkegaard
leads.species: London Plane or Oriental Plane (Platanus sp., not confirmed)
leads.location_hint: on a lawn somewhere in Assistens Kirkegaard, Norrebro
leads.reason: Multiple thin search-summary mentions of 'a preserved giant plane tree, possibly Denmark's largest' at Assistens Kirkegaard, also referenced as having 'iconic tree' status under Copenhagen's tree designation programme, but every page actually fetched this pass (kk.dk cemetery page, storyhunt.io guide) turned out to contain no tree detail at all when read directly, only the search engine's own AI summary asserted it. This is a real, promising lead (the cemetery is 500m-1km from the existing Botanisk Have/Kongens Have cluster, and holds Andersen's and Kierkegaard's graves) but needs a primary source located and fetched directly, not just a search summary, before verification. Do not treat the 'possibly Denmark's largest' claim as sourced; it was never traced to an origin this pass. UPDATE 2026-08-09: worked dendron.dk's full Assistens register (12 entries, IDs 1467-1478) this pass; no Platanus entry exists there. If this tree is real it is not in the Danish Dendrological Society's survey, so the lead still needs a different primary source (a Kobenhavns Kommune tree register or a direct site visit), not another web sweep.

leads.name: Kastellet ramparts trees (elm, linden, horse chestnut)
leads.species: mixed: elm, linden, horse chestnut, various fruit trees
leads.location_hint: the star-shaped rampart of Kastellet, Copenhagen
leads.reason: Well documented that Kastellet's ramparts were deliberately planted with these species from 1663 onward (root systems to bind the earthworks, timber reserve, sightline-blocking), per fredninger.dk and hovedstadshistorie.dk, and the fortification itself is intact and highly walkable, directly adjacent to the existing Kongens Have/Botanisk Have cluster. But this is a planting programme across an entire rampart, not one identifiable tree, so no single specimen could be pulled out from what this pass read. Needs either a specific named/measured veteran tree (a Danish Dendrological Society register entry, as with Thorvaldsen's Robinia, would solve this in one fetch) or a site visit/photo survey to pick one out.
leads.note_for_ensemble_test: Even at its best this is closer to 'a fortification planted with trees' than one collectible point; would need one genuinely standout specimen, not the rampart as a whole.

leads.name: Copenhagen 'evighedstraeer' (eternity trees) designation
leads.species: unspecified, designated per-tree by the municipality
leads.location_hint: municipal nature areas only, e.g. Utterslev Mose; not city parks or gardens
leads.reason: Real, verified municipal programme (Koebenhavns Kommune Traepolitik, adopted 2016; criteria PDF read this pass: tree must be over 100 years old, beech >150, oak >200, diameter >1m, or carry major biological/historic/aesthetic value; ~50 eternity trees expected citywide) but the source material found is policy and committee minutes, not a published list of the actual designated trees with names or coordinates. Also structurally off the city's core walkable cluster: eternity trees are designated ONLY in municipal nature areas (Utterslev Mose, Amager Faelled, Vestvolden etc.), which sit well outside the Kongens Have/Botanisk Have/Slotsholmen spine and would need their own day-trip framing per the 30-minute rule. Needs the municipality's actual GIS layer or published tree list, not the policy document, before this goes anywhere.

leads.name: Magnolie, Sølvløn, Gul fyr, Vortebirk, Nøddetaks (Japanese Nutmeg-yew), Assistens Kirkegård
leads.species: mixed (Magnolia sp.; Acer saccharinum, Silver Maple; Pinus ponderosa, Ponderosa Pine; Betula pendula, Silver Birch; Torreya nucifera, Japanese Nutmeg-yew)
leads.location_hint: all within Assistens Kirkegård, GPS given per-tree by dendron.dk (Individual_ID 1478, 1473, 1472, 1469, 1475)
leads.reason: All five are in the Danish Dendrological Society's register (Hans Erik Lund, 26-11-2019, GPS-verified, all alive/healthy) but no second independent source was found for any of them in this or the prior pass, and none stood out as more remarkable than the Assistens trees that did clear the bar. UPDATE 2026-08-09: the sixth tree in this group, Tretorn (Honey Locust, Individual_ID=1476), DID clear the bar this pass via a 1952 Danish Dendrological Society yearbook article (dendron.dk/aarsskrift/docs/6.pdf) that independently places a Gleditsia triacanthos in the same section (E) of Assistens, documented since 1941; shipped as cop_011, removed from this group. Also checked this pass: Torreya nucifera's species ID was tested against a Danish gardening source claiming only Torreya californica reliably survives outdoors in Denmark, but no source was found that actually names a Torreya at Assistens as californica rather than nucifera, so this is circumstantial doubt, not a conflicting second source; still a lead, not blocked.

leads.name: Frederiksberg Have remainder: Navr, Ær (x2) (dendron.dk Individual_ID 836, 838, 840)
leads.species: mixed (Acer campestre, Field Maple; Acer pseudoplatanus x2, Sycamore Maple)
leads.location_hint: all within Frederiksberg Have, GPS given per-tree by dendron.dk
leads.reason: Danish Dendrological Society register only (Hans Erik Lund, 12-10-2016, all alive), smaller girths than the two Frederiksberg Have trees delivered earlier (cop_009 the beech, cop_010 the oak). No second independent source chased this pass given the time budget. UPDATE 2026-08-09: the two Avnbøg (hornbeam) entries in this original group are no longer both leads. Individual_ID=842 is 'Suttetraeet', the pacifier tree, a well-known Copenhagen tradition (annual pacifier harvest since 2004, per frederiksbergliv.dk) independently confirming the register; shipped as cop_012, flagged because the register carries no age or girth data for it at all. Individual_ID=841, the other hornbeam, was not chased and remains a lead.

leads.name: Knudebøgen (Copper Beech), Assistens Kirkegård afd. A (dendron.dk Individual_ID=1470)
leads.location_hint: Assistens Kirkegård, NW corner of section A, near the wall between A and B+C, GPS 55.69106 12.55339 per dendron.dk
leads.reason: UPDATE 2026-08-09: re-checked this pass with targeted web searches ('Assistens Kirkegård kobberbøg/knudebøg/blodbøg', photo/deformation terms); still no second independent source. bennyfriisgunno.dk's detailed Assistens planting survey, which DID corroborate three other register trees this pass, does not name a copper beech among its listed species. Genuinely striking (severe graft-site deformation) but single-sourced; still a lead.

leads.name: Ceder (true cedar, Cedrus sp.), Assistens Kirkegård afd. A/B border (dendron.dk Individual_ID=1471)
leads.species: Cedar (Cedrus sp., species not specified by the register)
leads.location_hint: Assistens Kirkegård, 60m from Nørrebrogade, 10m from the wall between afd. A and B+C, GPS 55.69076 12.55274
leads.reason: Register data pulled this pass: 2.52m circumference, 16.5m tall, alive/healthy 2019, 'flot stamme' (handsome trunk), no cones autumn 2019 despite heavy seed-set in most other species that year. Species conflict UNRESOLVED: bennyfriisgunno.dk separately describes a 'Flodceder' (river cedar, almost certainly Thuja plicata / Western Redcedar rather than a true Cedrus) standing next to the Monkey Puzzle Tree in section A; per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md this is a fundamental disagreement (different genus, not just a naming variant), so per the brief's own rule this stays a lead rather than shipping flagged. Needs a site-specific photo or a register correction before either merging or separating these as two trees.

leads.name: The Catalpa of Kuglegarden
leads.location_hint: Kuglegarden, Arsenalvej, Holmen, Copenhagen (55.67825, 12.60056)
leads.reason: Held on ACCESS, not on evidence. The Dansk Traeregister carries it with a verified position (id 1860), 339 cm girth and 16.5 m, photographed by Hans Erik Lund whose permission we have. Kuglegarden is a former naval arsenal courtyard now leased to private tenants, and the sources disagree about whether the public may walk into the courtyard or only into the showrooms in business hours. Hard rule 10: we do not guess about access. One clear answer from the site itself or the tenants opens it, and the tree ships that day.

leads.name: The tallest beech in Denmark, Dyrehaven
leads.location_hint: North of Peter Lieps Hus, Dyrehaven, about 10 km north of Copenhagen. Peter Lieps Hus stands at 55.77760, 12.57702; the tree is somewhere north of it and is not pinned.
leads.reason: Would be a national height record and clears our bar on height alone: about 45 m against a species reference of 32 m built from 38 measured beeches, so roughly 141 percent. It is a LEAD and not a tree because it cannot be pinned. 'North of Peter Lieps Hus' covers a large stretch of beech forest, and a tall beech among beeches cannot be told apart without a coordinate, a photograph or a recognition line, which is the 2026-09-08 rule. Naturstyrelsen, which manages Dyrehaven, or Lund himself could give the position in one answer.
leads.source: Hans Erik Lund, who runs the Dansk Traeregister, by mail 2026-09-20: 'Denmarks highest beech (about 45 m): north to Peter Lieps House in Dyrehaven around 10 km north to Copenhagen. Info was given by the forester of Dyrehaven Friday 18. September 2026.'

leads.name: The thick Turkish hazel of Frederiksberg Hospital
leads.location_hint: South-eastern corner of the Frederiksberg Hospital grounds, north side of Nyelandsvej, about 30 m west of Nordre Fasanvej. The junction sits at 55.68428, 12.52466, so the tree is near 55.6843, 12.5242.
leads.reason: Pinnable and probably the strongest of his three tips. The Turkish hazel we already publish at Vestre Kirkegard stands at 210 cm, which is 68 percent of our species reference, and he calls this one 'very thick', so it likely goes over it. Needs a measured girth and a check that the hospital grounds are open, which most Danish hospital gardens are. Ask him for the girth: he measures these himself.
leads.source: Hans Erik Lund, who runs the Dansk Traeregister, by mail 2026-09-20: 'A very thick turkish hazel can be found here: South eastern corner of the Frederikserg Hospital area, Nyelandsvej north-side, around 30 m west of Nordre Fasanvej.'

leads.name: The pagoda tree of Ordrupgaard
leads.location_hint: Ordrupgaard museum grounds, Vilvordevej 110, Charlottenlund, about 5 km north of the city centre (museum at 55.76719, 12.56296)
leads.reason: Girth 3.91 m, thicker than the 3.15 m pagoda tree we are publishing at Rolighedsvej, which the register already calls remarkable at national level. The museum park is open to the public and free to walk, the building itself is ticketed. Needs a coordinate for the tree rather than the museum, and a second source.
leads.source: Hans Erik Lund, who runs the Dansk Traeregister, by mail 2026-09-20: 'A big Pagoda Tree (Styphnolobium (Sophora) japonicum) can be found at Ordrupgaard Museum 5 km north of Copenhagen Center. Girth 3,91.'

blocked.reason: CONFIRMED DEAD. Planted 1858 when the garden was founded (its oldest tree, 5 m circumference, described by fredninger.dk's older snapshot as the garden's thickest tree), but Danish Wikipedia's Landbohojskolens Have entry states plainly it 'blev faeldet i 2018 grundet svampeangreb, men traeets hovedstamme staar stadig tilbage' (was felled in 2018 due to fungal infection; only the main trunk stump remains). Never ship as a living entry. Recorded here so no future pass re-verifies it from the older, now-stale fredninger.dk description alone.

blocked.name: Bispebjerg Kirsebaeralle (Cherry Blossom Avenue), Bispebjerg Kirkegaard
blocked.species: Japanese flowering cherry (Prunus sp., likely Prunus serrulata / yedoensis cultivars)
blocked.reason: Genuinely famous (up to 150,000 visitors at peak bloom per tourism sources) and would be an easy sell, but it is a long avenue of many individual cherry trees along a cemetery path, not one collectible point or a compact famous ensemble with a single obvious place to stand; the trees themselves are also ordinary-aged flowering cherries (an ornamental planting), not ancient or individually remarkable specimens. Blocked under BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's explicit rule that 'an avenue or a whole wood is blocked', on the same logic as La Rambla's plane trees. Judged honestly per the brief's instruction, not defaulted.
